newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy seen issuing 17.0 trln lit BTP, CCT.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy seen issuing 17.0 trln lit BTP, CCT.

text.p: The Italian Treasury is expected on average to issue 17.0 trillion lire at its next medium and long term paper auctions against some 24.5 trillion lire maturing, a Reuter poll of economists showed.

"The Treasury can issue less paper than the amount that is maturing because the beginning of year auctions were large enough to give the Treasury a comfortable margin for the end of the year," one analyst said.

Last Friday the Treasury said it would issue a third tranche of September 1, 2003 floating rate certificates (CCT), with a 4.55 percent coupon, and a 13th tranche of July 1, 2006 fixed rate paper (BTP), with a 8.75 percent coupon. Settlement date for this paper is scheduled on Tuesday, October 1.

On Monday September 30 the Treasury will offer a new tranche of October 1, 1999 BTPs and September 15, 2001 BTPs, with coupons of 7.50 and 7.75 percent respectively, lower than 8.25 percent coupons on the previous series of Btps auctionned.
Settlement for these bonds is set for Wednesday, October 3.
In addition to 12.5 trillion lire of three year BTP and 12.0 trillion lire of CCTs, some 10.0 trillion lire of coupons come due at the beginning of October.
"The lower coupons will bring prices slightly under par value," one analyst said noting that this should not cause lower demand for the paper.
"This way, the Treasury is indicating that market rates are coming down, giving a positive signal for a discount rate cut," the analyst added.
Other analysts are more cautious on the lower coupons on the three year paper and note that it could cause "more subdued demand."

"The Treasury will try to exploit the still favourable environment for bonds ahead of the budget discussions," Bank of America said in a research note. The 1997 budget package is expected to be unveiled later this week.
